model_annotations.Bulgarian: This bar chart compares the accuracy (%) of five different reinforcement learning-based methods—DAPO+Self-reflection (blue solid), DAPO (blue striped), GRPO (orange striped), PPO+Self-reflection (dark green solid), and PPO (teal striped)—across three benchmark datasets: Mathverse, MMLU, and Physics. The vertical axis represents accuracy in percentage, ranging from 50% to 62% with tick marks every 2 percentage points. The horizontal axis lists the three datasets in order from left to right. For each dataset, the five methods are grouped together, with their bars arranged in the same order as defined in the legend. In Mathverse, DAPO+Self-reflection achieves the highest accuracy at approximately 56.2%, followed by SRPO (orange solid, ~55.8%), DAPO (~53.2%), GRPO (~53.4%), and PPO (~53.2%). In MMLU, DAPO+Self-reflection again leads at ~56.8%, followed by SRPO (~57.0%), DAPO (~56.0%), GRPO (~55.8%), and PPO (~54.6%). In Physics, DAPO+Self-reflection reaches the highest accuracy at ~61.2%, followed by SRPO (~60.8%), DAPO (~57.6%), GRPO (~58.2%), and PPO (~57.0%). The chart visually emphasizes that DAPO+Self-reflection consistently outperforms the other methods across all three datasets, with the largest performance gap observed in the Physics dataset.
